Market leadership has shifted:

Apple, $AAPL, has outperformed Nvidia, $NVDA, by 30.2 percentage points so far in November, putting it on track for its largest monthly outperformance since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

Since October 1st, $AAPL has outperformed $NVDA by 44.1 percentage points, putting it on track for its largest 2-month outperformance since July 2011.

$AAPL is also on pace to finish higher in 7 of the last 8 months and is up +31.3% year-to-date.

Apple has quietly become one of the biggest beneficiaries of the recent market rotation.

Back in the days charts were more clear... we hear a lot right?

Correct. With computerized trading, Global access and funds/market makers price action became more volatile. Breakouts are not as clean as before...

I agree. But this is the case in the widely traded names. 

Nothing stops you to search the non-popular names. The price charts are as clean as the old days. You don't need to trade NVDA, META or AMD. 

As breakout traders we are after directional movement no matter where.

I worked at different parts of the financial industry.

Analyst at a leading brokerage firm.
Analyst/fund manager, portfolio manager at semi-sovereign funds.
Portfolio manager at family offices.

I can tell you with confidence, the most advantaged individuals in financial sector are "part-time retail traders".

Note: if you are disciplined with great self control and operate not with instincts but with predefined rules, do not need to follow markets intraday, do not need more than 1 screen to run research and place orders, have the flexibility to step out of your office and engage in non-finance activities you are way ahead and with more clear mind than the trader who sits in front of 4 screens that are connected to a Bloomberg terminal.

For me the simple strategy is based on capturing trend periods out of well-defined consolidations. In this, I focus on breakouts through horizontal boundaries with min 3 touch points. No indicators. No volume. Pure price action out of a well-defined consolidation.

A sound risk management should have "on average" $ win / $ loss > 4 and can be profitable with win rates between 35%-45%. The asymmetry in finding setups to capture directional movement should aim these.

Build a strategy so simple (not depending on lines of codes) in your analysis but so sound in risk management that when all platforms are down, you can still function normally.

Inflationary is intensifying in Japan:

Japan’s Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) jumped +4.2% YoY in October, its largest annual increase since 1990, and far above expectations of +3.6%.

This index tracks domestic prices businesses charge each other for services, and serves as a key inflation metric in Japan.

MoM, the index rose +1.1%, up from +0.3% in the previous month and marking its biggest monthly increase in 6 months.

The latest surge was driven particularly by higher ocean freight transportation costs, leasing costs, and hotel charges.

Prices in transport and postal activities alone jumped +9.4% YoY in October, following an +8.4% increase in September.

Rising inflationary pressures are strengthening the case for a December rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

BREAKING: The Nasdaq 100 has recorded an average intraday range of 3.8% over the last 5 trading sessions, its highest 5-day volatility since April 2025.

This is also its 2nd-highest reading since the 2022 bear market, when it peaked at 4.0%.

On Wednesday alone, this figure rose to 4.2%, while on last Friday it surged to 5.7%, its widest single-session intraday trading range since April 9th, 2025.

By comparison, during the 2020 pandemic and the 2008 Financial Crisis, the Nasdaq 100 saw 5-day average intraday ranges as much as 7.7% and 8.9%, respectively.

The largest 5-day average intraday range in the Nasdaq 100 was recorded following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst, at 10.2% in January 2001.

Volatility across tech stocks is historically high.

The US Dollar is experiencing one of its strongest rallies in years:

The US Dollar Index has surged +7.0% over the last 9 months, its strongest 9-month rolling performance since November 2022.

This also marks its 2nd-strongest such run since October 2015.

Over the last 3 months alone, the US Dollar Index has risen +4.8%, its largest 3-month increase since December 2024.

Since its January 2026 low, the US Dollar Index is up +8.8%, to its highest level since April 2024.

Meanwhile, the EUR/USD is down -9.1% since its January high, to 1.1, near its lowest level since April 2025.

This comes as rising Fed rate hike expectations, strong US economic data, and record foreign demand for US stocks are all driving the currency higher.

The US Dollar is seeing a massive comeback this year.

Meanwhile, just 7 stocks saw a record $9.5 billion in CDS volume traded on average per week in September.

This represents a +425% increase from June and July levels.
